scores.accuracy_concern: Vaughn 2019 cohort was all adults in 43 Michigan hospitals (not an older-only sample) and the 5% rise in odds of adverse events per excess day is observational, so no causal verb; NICE NG138 advises 5 days for low-severity CAP and a review at 5 days for moderate/high severity, so 'most adults' needs the exact wording; the C. difficile age claim is still unverified.
scores.sharpen: State the population (adults of all ages with pneumonia, US) in one clause and show the two discharge lines side by side as the whole visual, since the wording change is the post.

scores.accuracy_concern: The four headings are editorial judgement, not a published standard; NICE NG27 wording on sharing information with the care home at the time of discharge needs checking; the CQC and qualitative sources on incomplete information are not yet found.
scores.sharpen: Anchor it to one sourced finding about what care home staff report missing at transfer, and cut the opening to one short sentence before the four questions.

scores.values_concern: Avoid reading as a criticism of End PJ Paralysis or its staff, or as downplaying deconditioning; the case for getting people up should stay strong.
scores.accuracy_concern: Kortebein studied 11 healthy volunteers, and acutely ill patients may lose more, so the slogan may understate as well as overstate; the ~1 kg lean leg mass loss (about 6%) can be converted into years of age-related loss, so 'an equivalence nobody measured' may be wrong; attribution of the slogan to Gill 2004 is unverified; it also sits awkwardly against the earlier E131 equivalence claim.
scores.sharpen: Frame it as 'what the ten days in bed study actually measured, in healthy volunteers' and say plainly that ill patients are likely to fare worse, so the correction strengthens rather than weakens the mobility message.

scores.accuracy_concern: The central practical claim (the ward may already have given that day's doses; weekly tablets' day may shift) is general practice without a named source; Alqenae 2020 prevalence estimates vary widely between studies and should not be given as one number.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the methotrexate or alendronate weekly-day example as the concrete hazard, and find one pharmacy or NICE NG5 source for recording last-dose times at transfer.

scores.accuracy_concern: Hold periods and restart processes vary by council, provider and nation (England and Scotland differ), and no published source yet supports the general claim; in some areas packages are held or restarted automatically, so the post could mislead.
scores.sharpen: Find one official or Healthwatch source that describes packages being released during admission, and phrase the rule as 'varies by area: ask your council' rather than implying a standard period.

scores.accuracy_concern: Roy 2005 is 2004 US academic-hospital data across all ages; physician unawareness (61.6%) was measured in a surveyed subset of potentially actionable results; the study did not show harm, which must be stated.
scores.sharpen: Tie it to older people by naming the results most often pending for them (cultures, B12, thyroid, histology) and give the named-owner line as the visual.

scores.values_concern: Families should not be left feeling they failed if the person dies in hospital or if home proves impossible; state that the plan can change and that home is one of several good places to die.
scores.accuracy_concern: The NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track is England only (Scotland ended NHS continuing healthcare in 2015 and uses different arrangements); the claim that some people die before rapid discharge happens has no source yet; BMJ Open Qual 2024 authors and findings need the full text.
scores.sharpen: Name the slowest usual step (equipment or community medicines) from the QI paper and give a single question per lane, with a Scotland-appropriate funding line or none.

scores.accuracy_concern: The urgent community response two-hour standard is England only; hospital at home availability varies; Shepperd 2021 found similar living-at-home and death outcomes in selected, stable patients, so 'similar outcomes' should be limited to those.
scores.sharpen: Keep the 'what we can and can't do tonight' two-column card, and add one sentence saying these services are not available everywhere so a 'no' is not the family's failure.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 'only modestly better than chance' line fits the administrative-data models (c 0.55 to 0.65) but models used at discharge reached 0.68 to 0.83; the 2011 review predates newer scores such as HOSPITAL and machine learning models, so a later review is needed.
scores.sharpen: Replace the c statistic with a plain ranking reading ('picks the right one of two patients about 6 times in 10') and name which kinds of score it applies to.

scores.accuracy_concern: NHS England has published 12 hours from arrival monthly since 2023, so 'has been counted' must be dated; official definitions pages could not be opened from this environment; ambulance handover time and Scottish definitions need official documents; not specific to older people.
scores.sharpen: Build it on one opened official document per clock (NHS England and PHS) and add one line on why older people are more exposed to the longest waits, or drop it.

scores.accuracy_concern: Bulger 2000 pneumonia estimate conflicts between results (OR 1.16) and conclusion (27%): quote only the mortality OR or the direction; Kehoe 2015 figures are 2013 TARN data and newer TARN reports exist; the undertriage claim from TARN 2017 is still to check.
scores.sharpen: Use the 1990 versus 2013 mechanism shift as the visual and close on one triage instruction (anticoagulant plus low fall means look for head and chest injury).

scores.values_concern: Do not frame hospital at home as a cheaper substitute or assume family carers absorb the work; state what it asked of households.
scores.accuracy_concern: The residential care relative risk 0.58 is adjusted and differs from the crude 5.7% versus 8.7% (about 0.66): give the absolute figures only; randomisation was 2:1 and participants were selected, stable, mean age 83.
scores.sharpen: Give the per 100 icon array only and add one verified sentence on carer outcomes from the trial report, so the 'what it asks of families' promise is kept.

scores.values_concern: Keep bed managers and ward staff out of the blame; the target is a measure that is not reported.
scores.accuracy_concern: Blay 2017 was one Australian hospital, all ages, 2008 to 2009 administrative data, with likely confounding by indication (sicker patients are moved more); 'routine NHS statistics do not report bed moves' is unverified; the night-move FOI claim has no source.
scores.sharpen: Say in one clause that sicker people are moved more so the link is not proof, and keep the countable measure (moves per stay, moves at night) as the call to action.

scores.accuracy_concern: The model adjusted for comorbidity, age, deprivation and crowding, not acute illness severity, so 'adjusted for illness' overstates and residual confounding remains; the 1 in 82 figure applies to delays beyond 6 to 8 hours from arrival and the comparison group needs the full text; all adult admissions, not older people only.
scores.sharpen: Drop 'illness' from the adjustment list, give the 1 in 82 figure with its comparison in plain words, and add the verified share of long waits experienced by older people.

scores.accuracy_concern: Dugaret 2012 is a single French emergency department and its figures need checking; NPSA RRR009 (2010) is old though still standard; the older-people waits figure is not yet sourced.
scores.sharpen: Keep the four labelled requests and add one sourced figure (ED pressure ulcer incidence by length of stay) so the post is more than common sense.

scores.accuracy_concern: Check the IDSA wording on how often fever is absent in serious infection (commonly quoted as 30 to 50% of frail older adults, not 'more than half'); thresholds differ by route (oral 37.8 single, 37.2 repeated; rectal 37.5); the guideline population is long-term care residents, and a baseline temperature is often unknown in the emergency department.
scores.sharpen: Add a practical line on where to find the baseline (care home charts, GP or previous admissions) so the habit is usable at the front door.

scores.accuracy_concern: RR 1.06 needs the control-group rate to give an absolute figure (roughly 3 more per 100 alive at home); most benefit came from ward-based trials, so the 'ward or team: unclear' point must follow the review wording; 2017 review, check for any update.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the absolute number of people per 100 more likely to be at home and use that as the visual, which will also lift the opening.

scores.accuracy_concern: Confirm that each effect estimate (length of stay -0.73 days, readmission RR 0.89, mortality RR 1.05) comes from the subgroup of older people admitted with a medical condition, not the whole review; readmission follow-up averaged three months.
scores.sharpen: Give readmission per 100 with the control rate, and name one thing the trials show discharge also depends on (home care availability) so modest effects lead to an action.

scores.accuracy_concern: The Loyd 2020 figure (about 30%) is a pooled prevalence of hospital-associated disability with varied definitions; 'criteria to reside' is England-specific; no source yet criticises the phrase 'medically fit', so the claim that others read it as 'well' is judgement.
scores.sharpen: Show the two note lines as the whole visual and mark the reading by families as the author's judgement, not a finding.

scores.values_concern: Avoid implying that social care staff or councils are at fault; describe the waiting person without assigning blame.
scores.accuracy_concern: Rojas-Garcia 2018 associations come mostly from moderate or low quality studies, and people who are delayed tend to be frailer, so confounding is likely; the professional-body criticism of 'bed blocking' is not yet sourced.
scores.sharpen: Put one plain sentence on confounding next to the list of harms and find the BGS or RCP statement before naming the term.

scores.accuracy_concern: Aminzadeh and Dalziel 2002 is an old review and emergency department interventions were inconclusive; PROFET (1999) findings were not consistently replicated in later trials, so it should not be presented as settled.
scores.sharpen: Replace the 2002 review with a recent systematic review or cohort of adverse outcomes after ED discharge in older people, and keep only the questions that evidence supports.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 5% to 79% range and 27.1% median are from 34 mostly single-centre studies using subjective criteria; Auerbach 2016 (about 27% potentially preventable) should be checked before it is used as confirmation.
scores.sharpen: Fill the placeholders with the verified range and median and add one example of a preventable cause a case review finds that a rate can't show.

scores.values_concern: Must not read as a case for keeping care home residents out of hospital to save beds; the resident's wishes and adequate monitoring come first.
scores.accuracy_concern: Loeb 2006 was Canadian, 2006, and the pathway included a research nurse and portable chest X-ray, which most UK care homes lack; hospitalisation figures are crude and the trial was not powered for mortality.
scores.sharpen: Put 'what the home needed to make this work' on the visual as prominently as the result, so families can ask whether their home has it.

scores.accuracy_concern: SAFER bundle wording on expected discharge date needs checking; Healthwatch 2015 is dated; Carers (Scotland) Act section 28 duty wording is unverified and overlaps C18-16.
scores.sharpen: Merge with C15-05 into a single 'questions to ask in the first two days' post, or give it a sourced figure on how little notice families report.

scores.accuracy_concern: Heslop 2014 covers south-west England deaths 2010 to 2012 and uses 'amenable to good-quality healthcare', which differs from LeDeR's 'avoidable'; median age at death was 64, so the geriatric framing must not imply these are mostly old-age deaths; the Equality Act does not extend to Northern Ireland.
scores.sharpen: Use the latest LeDeR figures for currency, keep Heslop for the sex gap, and focus the hospital checklist on older people with a learning disability admitted with frailty.

scores.accuracy_concern: Coleman 2006 was one US health system in 2002 to 2003; the four elements come from programme materials, not the trial abstract; replications in other settings have been mixed.
scores.sharpen: Show the 30-day and 90-day figures per 100 and name one UK or European test of the model, or say that none has been found.

allocation_reason: 25 of 26 candidates score 36 or more and 14 score 44.5 or more with complementary angles, sound sources and no disqualifying flags; the category is broad and central to geriatric medicine, so it can fill the top of the range.
balance_note: Top 14 split practitioners 5 (C15-16, 01, 11, 22, 18), both 5 (12, 14, 25, 17, 26) and public 4 (23, 07, 04, 15). The public posts cluster in ranks 8 to 14 because 'Ask this' ideas rest on guidance rather than trials, so a smaller allocation would lose public coverage first; keep at least four public posts. Within the top 14, three pairs are close in theme (12 and 23 on treatment outside hospital; 14 and 15 on emergency department waits; 18 and 26 on discharge interventions); they complement each other but should be spaced apart in the calendar. C15-19 or C15-20 can replace C15-18 or C15-26 if the discharge-trial pair feels repetitive.
